# Rayner explainers

> Step-through explainers made with Rayner. Each page has a JSON file beside it, from `describeExplainer`: every case and step, with its title, caption, the state the scene recorded, what the step changed, and the resting picture in words and drawn as text.

Each item links the page, gives the first sentence of its first caption, and links its JSON.

## Explainers

- [Why June brings polar day to Tromsø and winter to Sydney](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/seasons): Earth’s axis is tilted 23.44° from the normal to its orbit and points the same way all year, so the north end leans toward the Sun in June and away from it in December. JSON: [seasons.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/seasons.json)
- [Why stealing an authorization code is not enough](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/oauth-pkce): PKCE protects public clients, such as mobile and desktop apps, which cannot keep a client secret. JSON: [oauth-pkce.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/oauth-pkce.json)
- [Git names each object by the hash of its bytes](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/exgit): Git hashes a header (the type, the byte length and a zero byte) followed by the content. JSON: [exgit.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/exgit.json)
- [A token bucket refills when a request arrives](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/token-bucket): The bucket starts full at five tokens, and each accepted request spends one. allow(now) adds refill for the time since the last call, so no background timer runs. JSON: [token-bucket.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/token-bucket.json)
- [Four added lines and one rewritten put a KV cache in front of D1](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/mr-cache): getUser is a single D1 query, the outlined line, so the walked request goes from the handler straight to D1, and every lookup is a database read. JSON: [mr-cache.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/mr-cache.json)
- [One transition table drives both session histories](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/state-machine): A session starts idle, and the ring shows where it is. JSON: [state-machine.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/state-machine.json)
- [A ring buffer reuses freed slots and refuses a push when full](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ring-buffer): Head is the next value to pop; tail is the next slot to write. JSON: [ring-buffer.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ring-buffer.json)
- [How 2password finds a secret without showing it to the agent](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/2password): The agent needs to choose a secret without receiving its value. 2password first asks op for item titles: it can search those names and return a reference, then let op pass the value to the launched app. JSON: [2password.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/2password.json)
- [Running a command returns a new shell value](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/just-bash): This executable model follows the JustBash example: a pipeline transforms strings and a redirect writes an in-memory filesystem. JSON: [just-bash.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/just-bash.json)
- [A renewal rule written for 90-day certificates renews 45-day ones twice as often](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/cert-renewal): The CA/Browser Forum’s Baseline Requirements cap how long a publicly trusted TLS certificate may be valid. JSON: [cert-renewal.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/cert-renewal.json)
- [Le quotient familial divise le revenu avant le barème, et son plafond reprend l’excédent](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/quotient-familial): Un couple marié ou pacsé, un enfant, déclare 65 673,88 € de revenu net imposable pour 2024. JSON: [quotient-familial.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/quotient-familial.json)
- [Arc<T> is Send and Sync only when T already is](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/send-sync): Send asks whether a value can move to another thread. JSON: [send-sync.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/send-sync.json)
- [A GTFS route never runs; its trips do, on the dates their service_id allows](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gtfs): The Demo Transit Authority’s sample feed contains routes even on dates when none of their trips run. JSON: [gtfs.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gtfs.json)
- [A one-integer Postgres row takes 36 bytes of an 8 KB page, and a bigint row takes the same](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pg-page): By default Postgres stores a table in pages of 8192 bytes, and every page starts with a 24-byte header. JSON: [pg-page.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pg-page.json)
- [externalTrafficPolicy: Local keeps the client’s address but splits traffic by node, not by pod](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/traffic-policy): A Service of type LoadBalancer: a cloud load balancer sends outside requests to the nodes, and rules that kube-proxy writes on each node hand every request to a pod. JSON: [traffic-policy.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/traffic-policy.json)
- [str.isdigit() accepts 128 characters that int() rejects](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/isdigit): The Unicode Character Database gives each of these a numeric value. JSON: [isdigit.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/isdigit.json)
- [Changing one meeting of a weekly series stores another VEVENT with the same UID](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ical-recurrence): Alice’s calendar app saves her stand-up as one VEVENT. JSON: [ical-recurrence.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ical-recurrence.json)
- [A new 1 TiB ext4 filesystem lets users write 93% of it; the 5% root reserve is nearly three times all its metadata](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ext4-space): mke2fs.conf sets 4096-byte blocks, so 1 TiB is 268,435,456 blocks in 8,192 groups of 32,768. JSON: [ext4-space.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/ext4-space.json)
- [With trust proxy set to 2, an attacker who skips the CDN can make Express report any client IP](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/trust-proxy): Requests are meant to reach Express through a CDN and then a load balancer, but the load balancer also accepts connections from the internet, so an attacker can skip the CDN. JSON: [trust-proxy.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/trust-proxy.json)
- [14 of Tailwind 4’s 17 coloured 500 shades lie outside sRGB; none lie outside Display P3](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/tailwind-gamut): Tailwind CSS 4.3.3’s theme.css writes all 286 palette shades as oklch(L C h): lightness, chroma (how far from grey) and hue angle. JSON: [tailwind-gamut.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/tailwind-gamut.json)
- [Each of six first-time users gave up on a GNOME Files task, every time in the menus](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gnome-files): Researchers for GNOME’s design team watched six people who had never used GNOME, aged 21 to 47, try eleven tasks in test builds of Files 47. JSON: [gnome-files.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/gnome-files.json)
- [WCAG 2.2 at level AA is 55 success criteria: 20 Perceivable, 20 Operable, 13 Understandable, 2 Robust](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/wcag-map): WCAG 2.0 (December 2008) sorts its success criteria under 4 principles and 12 guidelines. JSON: [wcag-map.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/wcag-map.json)

## How these are made

- [How one scene program becomes a page, pictures and a trace](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/lantern): How can one scene make both an interactive page and the stills and trace that inspect it? JSON: [lantern.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/lantern.json)
- [What changes when Lantern’s live player becomes a prebuilt page?](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/fork): What must change to send a scene as one HTML page instead of running it for each request? JSON: [fork.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/fork.json)
- [How a Mermaid verifier checks and repairs flowchart branches](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/agentic-mermaid): An agent drew two routes out of Cached but did not say which means yes. JSON: [agentic-mermaid.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/agentic-mermaid.json)
- [Why Rayner measures glyphs before drawing text](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/glyph): Why can the same word take different space in two fonts? JSON: [glyph.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/glyph.json)
- [A font’s advance places the next word](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/font-metrics): These letters are EB Garamond, explicitly requested by the scene. JSON: [font-metrics.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/font-metrics.json)
- [Choose where a panel starts](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/layout-direction): Start is the right card; End is the left card. JSON: [layout-direction.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/layout-direction.json)
- [How a hand-drawn timeline keeps its labels inside fixed boxes](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pen-and-pencil): A simulated hand makes every stroke a little different. JSON: [pen-and-pencil.json](https://oshineye.dev/projects/rayner/pen-and-pencil.json)
